::: {.why}
Before the GARCH family it is worth knowing that the simplest possible recursive estimator captures most of the forecastable variation, because it sets the bar the rest of the week has to clear.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the EWMA recursion and say what the decay parameter corresponds to in terms of effective sample size.
- Report the out-of-sample forecast accuracy of EWMA against a rolling window at three horizons.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement both estimators in qlib/vol.py: a rolling standard deviation and an EWMA with an explicit halflife. Then compare their one-day-ahead forecasts against realised absolute returns using mean squared error and the QLIKE loss, over a long out-of-sample period.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Tune the decay honestly, out of sample: fit the halflife on the first half of the sample and evaluate on the second, then report what the in-sample optimal halflife would have been. The gap between the two is the size of the overfitting you avoided.
:::
:::
